title: Service Sensitivity: Eval SLA Matrix and Prioritization Playbook
author: Priya Menon
body:
Summary
-------
This playbook defines a service-sensitivity driven evaluation (eval) SLA matrix and a reproducible prioritization algorithm for scheduling eval resources across Redwood’s eval harness. The goal is to ensure that eval coverage maps to business risk, customer-facing SLOs, and cost budgets while keeping the model onboarding and regression-triage workflows predictable and auditable.

Goals
- Make eval prioritization deterministic and defensible.
- Align eval cadence and fidelity to service-level sensitivity (impact if degraded).
- Provide clear onboarding steps and triage triggers tied to measurable thresholds.
- Reduce token spend waste by automatically degrading eval fidelity when budget pressure is high.

Scope
- Applies to all eval jobs that run on the central eval harness (shadow runs, synthetic probes, slice scans).
- Includes quantization, KV-cache, and latency sensitivity checks necessary for production promotion.
- Not intended for research-only experiments or unconstrained hyperparameter sweeps.

Definitions
- Service Sensitivity: categorical label (Critical / Important / Low) representing customer impact if model quality regresses.
- Eval SLA: target cadence and minimum fidelity required (e.g., sample size, annotation depth, pass thresholds).
- Fidelity Delta: allowed degradation in measured quality (e.g., 1.5% absolute accuracy drop, or 0.02 loss increase).
- Eval Budget Unit (EBU): accounting unit mapped to token/compute costs used for budget enforcement.

Service Sensitivity Matrix (canonical)
| service_tier | example_product_area | business_impact | SLO_target | eval_cadence | min_sample_size | allowed_fidelity_delta | cost_priority |
|--------------|----------------------|-----------------|-----------:|-------------:|-----------------:|----------------------:|--------------:|
| Critical     | customer-chat, billing-automation | revenue-impact, regulatory | p99 latency < 150ms; accuracy > 98% | daily smoke + weekly slice | 2,000 probes/week | 0.5% absolute | high |
| Important    | search-relevance, support-assist | user-satisfaction | p99 latency < 250ms; accuracy > 94% | weekly full + triage-on-alert | 800 probes/week | 1.5% absolute | medium |
| Low          | internal-summarization, discovery | internal efficiency | p99 latency < 400ms; accuracy > 88% | monthly sample | 200 probes/month | 3.0% absolute | low |

How to use this matrix
1. Identify service_tier during product onboarding (see Onboarding Checklist below).
2. Map onboarding label to the canonical matrix. If product deviates, attach a short exception with owner approval.
3. The eval scheduler uses the matrix to assign priority weight and minimum EBU per eval job.

Prioritization algorithm (high level)
1. Compute base_priority = f(service_tier) where Critical=100, Important=60, Low=20.
2. Adjust for recency: recent_regression_hit -> +30 score.
3. Adjust for rollout stage: canary -> +20, GA -> +0.
4. Adjust for cost pressure: if cluster_utilization > 85% -> scale priorities by 0.6 for Low and 0.9 for Important (Critical unaffected).
5. Final_score = base_priority + adjustments. The scheduler orders eval runs by Final_score descending.

Example priority weights table
- Critical: base 100, min EBU 50/week
- Important: base 60, min EBU 20/week
- Low: base 20, min EBU 5/month

Eval scheduling policies
- Preemption: a Critical eval can preempt an Important or Low eval if Final_score delta > 30. Preempted jobs are checkpointed and requeued.
- Graceful fidelity scaling: when budget < 20% of expected monthly EBU, reduce per-job sample_size by 50% for Low tier and 25% for Important tier (never for Critical).
- Canary window: for any new model promotion, mandatory canary eval runs (Critical/Important: 72-hour window; Low: 7-day).

Onboarding checklist (model/service)
- Product owner declares service_tier and lists primary routes.
- Attach representative prompt families and failure slices (minimum 10 examples per slice).
- Provide acceptance metrics and guardrails (latency, accuracy, hallucination rate).
- Reserve an initial eval budget (EBU) for the first 30 days.
- Register contact and escalation path in the ticket and link to related pages.

Rollout and regression triage flow (operational steps)
1. Pre-promotion: run the canary eval suite. If any sentinel falls outside the allowed_fidelity_delta, block promotion.
2. Promotion: if canary passes, schedule staged rollout with telemetry hooks.
3. Monitoring: continuous probes at the cadence per matrix. Alert thresholds: fidelity_delta > allowed_fidelity_delta OR p99 latency > SLO_target + 20%.
4. On alert: run the fast triage runner (see "Fast Triage Runner" steps below). If triage confirms regression, rollback to previous model version and open a regression incident.

Fast Triage Runner (playbook)
1. Reproduce the failure on the same seed and prompt set used in probe. Capture full model output and tokens.
2. Run stratified slice checks (length, role, user-intent, localization).
3. Compare outputs to the last-known-good snapshot using metrics: accuracy, BLEU-like semantic overlap, embedding-distance drift.
4. If discrepancy localized to quantized artifact or KV cache mismatch, tag as "runtime-fidelity" and escalate to Serving Runtime.
5. If discrepancy appears model-internal (behavior change across many slices), tag as "model-regression" and escalate to Model-Onboarding/Research.
6. Attach artifacts to the regression ticket and set severity using the regression-impact-index.

Telemetry & metrics to emit (minimum)
- eval:probe_id, model_version, seed, prompt_family, slice_id, timestamp, latency_ms, tokens_in, tokens_out, score_primary, score_secondary, pass/fail_flag
- infra: cluster_utilization_pct, avg_gpu_mem_util_pct, queue_wait_seconds
- ownership: owner_team, contact_pager, runbook_link

Configuration table (scheduler knobs)
| knob | description | recommended default |
|------|-------------|---------------------|
| max_parallel_jobs | maximum concurrent eval runners per cluster | 120 |
| budget_headroom_pct | fraction of monthly EBU to keep unspent for emergency | 10% |
| fidelity_scaling_threshold_pct | cluster utilization at which fidelity scaling kicks in | 85% |
| preemption_score_delta | score delta required to preempt a running job | 30 |

Sample eval job YAML (example)
---
job_name: "billing-chat-slice-smoke"
service_tier: "Critical"
model_version: "rwd-v1-2026-03"
cadence: "daily-smoke"
sample_size: 2000
min_pass_rate: 0.98
budget_units: 60
owner: "payments-platform-team"
---

Notes on cost accounting
- Map EBU to real billing using the Eval Budgeting service: 1 EBU ≈ 10k tokens on average shadow traffic in our current fleet. This mapping is reviewed quarterly.
- When an eval run triggers a regression triage, additional EBUs are allocated from the emergency reserve; these are reconciled at the end of the incident.

Ownership and contacts
- Eval harness owner: eng-evals (primary oncall via #eng-evals)
- Regression triage lead: Applied ML (applied-ml-oncall)
- Serving runtime escalation: eng-serving-runtime oncall

Example scenarios
1) Canary failure for Critical chat model: immediate block, run Fast Triage Runner, if tagged runtime-fidelity -> serve fallback variant and open P1 with Serving Runtime; if tagged model-regression -> rollback + P1 for research.
2) Budget pressure during month-end: fidelity scaling reduces Low/Important sample sizes; Critical runs maintain full fidelity. Notify owners and pro-rate release schedules.

Appendix A — common queries
- Find probes failing in last 24h: SELECT probe_id, service, score_primary, timestamp FROM eval_probes WHERE pass=false AND timestamp > now() - interval '24 hours';
- Compute average EBU spend per service_tier: SELECT service_tier, sum(budget_units) FROM eval_jobs WHERE month = '2026-02' GROUP BY service_tier;

Appendix B — automation snippets
- Requeue command (cli): rwd-evalctl requeue --job-id 12345 --priority 95
- Snapshot compare (python): rwd_eval_tools.compare_snapshots('snapshot_prev.json', 'snapshot_now.json', metrics=['accuracy','embed_distance'])

Change log
- 2026-01-12: Created initial playbook (Priya Menon).
- 2026-02-20: Added fidelity-scaling algorithm and YAML job sample; clarified telemetry fields (Ethan Chung).

Related artifacts and readouts
- Weekly eval budget report (retained in /reports/eval-budget/).
- Regression-impact-index methodology (see related_pages).

Owners and next steps
- Owners: eng-evals (policy), applied-ml (triage), product-owners (service tier declarations).
- Next step: schedule a quarterly review to tune base_priority and EBU mapping; create a dashboard for Final_score heatmap.

If you are onboarding a model, start at the "Onboarding checklist" section and open an onboarding ticket with ownership details.
